title: How to mount cross-stitch in a hoop for display
subtitle: Finishing a small piece in its hoop for wall hanging or gifting
excerpt: Mounting a cross-stitch piece in its hoop for display is the simplest finishing method. The stitching stays in the hoop it was worked in, the fabric is trimmed to a neat circle, and the back is closed with a fabric circle or gathered running stitch. The hoop hangs from the screw on a wall or sits on a small stand.
sourceNotes: Hoop display finishing method. Standard guidance in major cross-stitch publisher guides.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads.

content.text: Mounting a finished piece in its hoop requires no framing equipment and gives a clean, immediate result. The
is kept taut in the hoop, the border is trimmed or gathered to the back, and the back is covered with a fabric circle. The piece hangs from the screw at the top of the hoop.

Mount the finished and washed piece in a clean wooden or bamboo hoop, centering the design in the hoop. Tighten the screw firmly. If the hoop has already marked the fabric from stitching, wash the piece before mounting in the display hoop.
Trim the fabric border to 2-3 cm beyond the hoop's inner ring. Do not trim closer; you need enough border to fold to the back.
Thread a needle with a doubled length of strong thread and work a running stitch around the fabric circle, about 1 cm from the outer edge of the Aida. Keep the stitches even.

Pull the running stitch to gather the fabric border to the back of the hoop's inner ring. The gathers should lie flat against the inner ring and the front of the design should remain taut and smooth. Tie off the gathering thread.

Cut a circle of felt or lining fabric to fit the back of the inner ring. Sew or glue it over the gathered back to cover the raw edges. The back should be neat and the screw at the top should be positioned for hanging.

items.symptom: The gathers pull the design off-centre or create puckers visible from the front
items.cause: The gathering stitch was too close to the hoop ring, or the gathers were not distributed evenly.
items.fix: Loosen the gathering thread, even out the gathers around the full circle before pulling tight. Ensure the design stays centred as you tighten; check the front as you go.

items.symptom: The hoop wobbles when hung on the wall
items.cause: The screw mechanism is at the wrong position on the hoop to hang flat.
items.fix: The screw should be at the 12 o'clock position. If it isn't, remount the piece in the hoop with the screw repositioned. You can also add a ribbon or cord to the screw as a hanging loop to gain more flexibility in how the piece hangs.

content.text: A hoop-mounted piece is also a straightforward gift. A finished design in a small hoop needs no extra materials from the recipient; it hangs immediately. For a neater result, use a wooden hoop rather than a plastic one, as wood holds the screw firm and looks cleaner on a wall.
